title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: PME Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Pro Medicus Limited from time to time. Subject to the same substantive dealing rules as employees; additionally bound by Corporations Act and Listing Rule notifiable interest obligations and a letter agreement with the company.

tiers.name: PME Employees
tiers.description: All persons engaged by or in the business of any member of the PME Group, expressly including key management personnel (AASB 124) and employees performing duties for Visage Imaging Inc or Visage Imaging GmbH. No sub-tiering by seniority.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman is the approver for out-of-window dealings by everyone else, can shorten Trading Windows and can bar named individuals from dealing; for the Chairman's own dealings the Board approves.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or Chairman may from time to time declare any other period to be a Blackout Period; the Company Secretary notifies Directors and Employees of the precise opening and closing dates (so not confidential as to existence). Separately the Chairman may reduce the length of any Trading Window, and may notify any one or more Directors or Employees that they cannot Deal during part or all of a Trading Window.

rules.detail: No express derivatives prohibition. PME Securities expressly include any derivative of PME shares or securities, naming equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not; to apply for, acquire, convert or dispose of one (or agree to do so) is a Dealing. An OTC put and written call therefore require the section 8.b) pre-dealing notification and Company Secretary confirmation, must fall in a Trading Window (or have Chairman approval), and are barred in Blackout Periods and while holding Inside Information.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: The policy contains no hedging prohibition and no definition of hedging or of limiting economic risk. 'Hedges' appear only as a category of PME Securities, so entering a hedge is a Dealing subject to the ordinary window and clearance machinery. No distinction is drawn between vested, unvested or restricted plan securities; section 12 defers to the rules of the Pro Medicus Share Plan and Option Plan, which are not part of this document and may impose their own hedging ban.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Nothing in the policy prohibits hedging of unvested or performance-hurdled plan securities; the only overlay is an undefined obligation to comply with the rules of the relevant incentive plan, which are external to the policy.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collars are not named. A collar or prepaid forward is a derivative of PME Securities and an agreement to dispose, so it is a Dealing requiring the pre-dealing notification, no Inside Information confirmation, Company Secretary clearance and execution within 7 days, inside a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Deal or Dealing means, in relation to any PME Security, to apply for, acquire, convert or dispose of that PME Security, or agreeing to, inciting, procuring or inducing any person or entity to do so.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned and is not listed in the Dealing definition; only the general insider trading, window and clearance rules would apply to any disposal.
Securities lending is not mentioned and is not within the Dealing definition, which is limited to applying for, acquiring, converting or disposing of a PME Security.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives of PME shares settled by cash, so they fall within PME Securities and dealing in them requires the section 8.b) clearance and a Trading Window. No speculative or short-term trading ban exists to catch them separately.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of the above ... whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly contemplated and not prohibited. The only obligation is disclosure: after a Dealing, full details must be given in writing to the Company Secretary including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities. Entering the margin loan is not itself a Dealing under section 14.c), so no prior clearance is imposed on the loan as such.
rules.evidence: the relevant PME Director or PME Employee must provide in writing full details of the Dealing to the Company Secretary, including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities.

rules.detail: Granting security over PME Securities is not prohibited and is not a Dealing (the definition covers only applying for, acquiring, converting or disposing). 'Other security arrangement affecting those securities' is named only in the post-dealing disclosure obligation to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities.

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing in respect of PME Securities of any kind, whether margin lending or other. The policy's sole treatment is the requirement to disclose any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting the securities when reporting a Dealing to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, no buy/sell window restriction, no intention test and no ban on speculative or short-term dealing.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (advice that there is no known reason to preclude the proposed Dealing), who must pass the notice to the Board; the Chairman for any Dealing outside a Trading Window
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (full details of the Dealing, including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities); plus Corporations Act and ASX Listing Rule notifiable interest disclosure and the director's letter agreement with Pro Medicus
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Following the Dealing'); statutory director notifications on their own timetable
clearance.evidence: advise the Company Secretary in writing of their intention to Deal in PME Securities (who must then pass that information to the Board); confirm in writing that they do not hold Inside Information; and have been advised by the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the proposed Dealing. Any Dealing must occur within 7 days of being so advised.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (advice that there is no known reason to preclude the proposed Dealing); the Chairman for any Dealing outside a Trading Window
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (full details of the Dealing, including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities)
clearance.evidence: Before Dealing in PME Securities, irrespective of whether it is in a Trading Window or with the prior written approval of the Chairman ... all PME Directors and PME Employees must: advise the Company Secretary in writing of their intention to Deal in PME Securities

clearance.approver: the Board (for the Chairman's own out-of-window Dealings); Company Secretary confirmation still applies to every Dealing
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (full details, including any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities)
clearance.evidence: Dealings in PME Securities outside a Trading Window are only permitted with the prior written approval of the Chairman (or, in the case of the Chairman, with the approval of the Board)

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Board in the case of the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: Dealings in PME Securities outside a Trading Window are only permitted with the prior written approval of the Chairman (or, in the case of the Chairman, with the approval of the Board), in each case: where there are exceptional circumstances (such as severe financial hardship); and the relevant PME Director or PME Employee is not aware of, and confirms in writing to the Board that they are not aware of, any Inside Information relating to PME Group.

financing_disclosure: PME Directors and PME Employees; trigger: following each Dealing in PME Securities; to the Company Secretary; deadline unspecified ('Following the Dealing'); content: full details of the Dealing including details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities

PME Directors; trigger: notifiable interests and Dealings generally; to the ASX/company under the Corporations Act and Listing Rules and under the director's letter agreement with Pro Medicus; deadline as prescribed by those requirements

external_documents: Any other employee incentive scheme rules from time to time
Letter agreement between each PME director and Pro Medicus relating to notifiable interests and notification of Dealings
exemption_authority: The Chairman (the Board in the case of the Chairman) may give prior written approval for a Dealing outside a Trading Window where there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship and the person confirms in writing to the Board that they hold no Inside Information; approval and any conditions (including disclosure) are entirely at the Chairman's or Board's discretion and the Dealing must occur within 7 days. No approval can override the Blackout Period prohibition in section 9 on its face, and the Board must approve any amendment to the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no prohibition on hedging, margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling or short-term dealing; the only reference to financing is the post-dealing disclosure of 'any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting those securities'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is not banned, so the structure turns entirely on window timing, Company Secretary clearance and disclosure rather than on any substantive prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PME Securities include any derivatives of PME shares and securities (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs, cash-settled or physically settled, are PME Securities, so each of entry, roll, unwind and settlement is a separate Dealing needing its own clearance and window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing is generally confined to three 30-day Trading Windows: after the full-year results, after the half-year results and after the AGM.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There are only about 90 dealing days a year, and the Chairman can shorten any window, so collar execution and any unwind must be scheduled tightly against the results and AGM calendar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Dealing must occur within 7 days of being so advised (and within 7 days of approval where the Chairman has approved an out-of-window Dealing).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete inside a 7-day clearance life or the clearance must be re-obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Dealing ... must comply with any conditions (including disclosure) which may be imposed by the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman, the Board). Any approval given or conditions imposed are within the discretion of the Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chairman can attach open-ended conditions, including public disclosure of the collar, as the price of any out-of-window execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ad hoc blackouts and window truncation
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman can, as he or she deems appropriate, reduce the period of any Trading Window from time to time ... the Board or Chairman may, from time to time, declare any other period to be a 'Blackout Period'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar unwind, roll or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice by a declared Blackout Period or a truncated window, so the documentation needs cash settlement or deferral mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees who acquire PME Securities under the Pro Medicus Share Plan, Pro Medicus Option Plan or any other employee incentive scheme from time to time must also comply with the rules of that Plan when Dealing in those securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging and encumbrance bans over unvested or plan-held shares may sit in the plan rules, which are not in this policy and must be diligenced separately before collaring plan shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to all PME Directors and PME Employees. There is no definition of associates, and no extension to spouses, dependants, controlled entities or trusts.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On its face the policy does not reach a family trust or controlled company holding the shares, though the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition and directors' notifiable interest obligations still bite.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Strict compliance with this policy is a condition of employment. Breaches of this policy will be subject to disciplinary action, which may include termination of employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale in a Blackout Period would be an unapproved Dealing by the borrower with dismissal risk, even though the policy is silent on forced sales.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2011 insider-trading document with no substantive prohibitions on hedging, derivatives, margin lending or secured financing. Both collar legs are PME Securities because the definition expressly captures equity swaps, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not, so entering, rolling, unwinding and settling the collar are each Dealings that require prior written notice of intention to the Company Secretary, a written confirmation of no Inside Information, and advice from the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the Dealing, with execution inside 7 days. Dealings must fall within one of the three 30-day Trading Windows after the full-year results, half-year results and AGM, outside the two four-week Blackout Periods and any ad hoc Blackout the Board or Chairman declares, and the Chairman may shorten a window or bar an individual; out-of-window execution needs the Chairman's (or for the Chairman, the Board's) approval on exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, subject to any conditions including disclosure. The secured loan is not itself a Dealing and is not prohibited, but full details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting the shares must be reported in writing to the Company Secretary after the Dealing, and directors must also meet their notifiable interest obligations and their letter agreement with the company. The main residual risks are the narrow dealing calendar with no forced-sale carve-out, and the rules of the Pro Medicus Share and Option Plans, which are incorporated by reference and may impose hedging or encumbrance restrictions on plan shares that this policy does not.
